arguments.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE isolated production pixel-art map image, CHAR001 Hero, idle, frame 01. Input 1 is the STRICT original character identity poster: extract design identity only, do not copy poster composition, captions or other views. Preserve brown tousled hair, blue eyes, blue and cream layered coastal clothes, shell necklace, coral ornaments, blue arm markings, decorated sword, sandals. true right facing profile, nose and toes toward right edge. neutral stance, feet fixed. Premium handcrafted crisp pixel clusters, restrained coherent palette, clean outlines, no blur, antialiasing or painterly rendering. Square-grid player-facing elevated 3/4 RPG map camera; readable compact proportions and silhouette compatible with 64x64 floor grid. Target native canvas 96x96, transparent RGBA. Design the pixels at native scale; if larger renderer output is needed use integer-enlarged native pixel blocks. Preserve full silhouette, head, weapon, feet with no clipping. Ground contact anchor [48, 90]; leave margins. Warm upper-left light. Additional reference is same-character prior frame for identical scale/costume only; CHANGE limbs and secondary motion as requested, never duplicate a static pose. No floor, cast shadow, background, poster, border, text, labels, collage, sprite sheet, multiple poses, extra character, or checkerboard. Exactly ONE image of this single asset/frame. CRITICAL NATIVE SPRITE DESIGN: compact MAP SPRITES of original poster define proportions, NOT tall key art. Design on underlying 96x96 logical pixel grid, 1-3 native pixel clusters. Elevated 3/4 camera shows top of head. NOT a detailed illustration shrunk down. Large readable head, exactly 3 heads tall overall, short stout torso and legs. Head about 25 native pixels; body height about 78. No realistic adult proportions. Preserve anatomical asymmetry: blue marking stays on the CHARACTER LEFT upper arm; sword stays in the CHARACTER RIGHT hand. Do not mirror the costume or move the marking to the other arm to make it visible. In right-facing profile the marking is on the far shoulder and may be occluded.
